note: Skeptic Shark · future-maintainer angle. Reviewed only the draft text (changelog is non-informative noise and not treated as a finding target). Severities limited to issues that either break later operators’ ability to ship the North Star honestly or leave an executable hole a future wave author will fill with guesswork.

findings.section: All phase headers + overview paragraph + E4 / John-in-the-loop cross-refs
findings.criterion: open/run/stop/restart + Doctor/attach without dead controls; every health/usage/diagnose surface works E2E or named-fails; cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: Headers are labeled `Phase 1 — Phase 0`, `Phase 2 — Phase 1`, … while body prose, E4, dependency rules, and the overview still say `Phase 0` / `Phase 1` / `Phases 0–2` without defining which numbering system is canonical. A future maintainer (or Foreman sub-agent) asked to “finish Phase 1 before surface waves” cannot tell whether that means Ground Truth, Capability Inventory, or Enabling Machinery. Wrong phase skip is exactly how Retry/Diagnose get wired without inventory transcripts, cost surfaces render without the Rollup Evidence Gate, and the end-to-end trace schema is applied after surfaces already shipped. Dual labels without a single authoritative ID map are not documentation style — they are an executable ambiguity that will reintroduce dead controls and fabricated dollars under the plan’s own dependency order.

findings.criterion: dead control / silent zero / mislabelled empty avoided by evidence-before-wiring; S1 is the only NS declaration
findings.message: The plan states the wave list is **not final until Phase 1 completes** and that surface waves are written from inventory verdicts — but it never names the artifact, owner, freeze gate, or doc-trio update procedure for that re-write. A future Stage-2/Foreman maintainer therefore either (a) invents waves mid-run without a second approval, or (b) runs a plan that cannot yet list the work that implements Doctor, attach, cost, restart, preview, cadence. Invented waves absorb “build it” into surface work (the failure mode the inventory was supposed to prevent) or omit a control entirely so S1 is the first time anyone notices. “Waves after inventory” without a **named re-plan freeze** (who edits which file, what John signs, what becomes immutable) is not honest sequencing — it is an escape hatch back into ad-hoc scope, which the exit register does not even list as an exit.

findings.criterion: John can open/run/stop/restart real work including Doctor diagnose — surfaces must ship, not only harnesses
findings.message: E4 fires “if Phases 0–2 have not completed by the point at which surface work must start,” but that point is never a calendar date, wall-clock budget, wave index, or John-signed milestone. The draft correctly names instrumentation overrun as a **likely** failure that leaves Diagnose dead under an excellent conformance suite — then leaves the only mitigation (E4) without a falsifiable trigger a future orchestrator can evaluate. Without a concrete “surface work must start by X” predicate, E4 will either never fire (harness eats the build → dead controls) or fire by informal panic (load-bearing items quietly drop → silent zeros and unbound honesty claims). A future-maintainer rule that cannot be applied without reinterpreting “must start” is not a budget; it is prose.

findings.section: Phase 1 — Phase 0 (verification task triple; collaborator smoke; cost_state isolation)
findings.criterion: real Anchor work referent; nothing ships to v1.1.x collaborators; cost never fabricates dollars
findings.message: The draft hard-blocks Wave 1 on a still-blank TASK-NAME / path / command / engines / John confirmation block; requires a “named v1.1.x collaborator” and check that are not named; and requires a plan-time cost_state ↔ branch-isolation resolution that is still a question. A future maintainer inheriting an “approved” Master Plan with those holes has no shared referent for “real work,” no collaborator isolation protocol to run after shared-artifact writes, and no written isolation answer before cost_state migration. The plan’s own words say unfilled verification fields make **every** acceptance criterion unfalsifiable — so leaving them blank in the draft under review means the honesty framework is not yet executable, only described. Approving incomplete plan-time facts is how later waves invent a task, skip collaborator smoke, or cosmetic-label cost under isolation pressure — all North-Star violations the exit register was written to prevent.

findings.topic: named-state vocab vs failure tables unmapped
findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 (named-state vocabulary; cost_state; failure-state table; attach reason enum)
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; every health/usage/diagnose surface named-fails honestly; cost labelling never from numeric zero
findings.message: The plan invents at least three parallel state systems — shared UI vocabulary (`measured/pending/unknown/empty/zero/unmeasured/failed/unavailable/unclassified`), `cost_state` enum (`measured/subscription_covered/free_tier/unmeasured/measurement_failed`), and per-wave failure-state tables (attach reasons, Doctor depths, preview classifications) — and never defines ownership, mapping, or amendment rules between them. A future surface-wave author will mint local labels that “look distinct” while the shared primitive still says `unknown`, recreating mislabelled empties and ambiguous zeros the North Star forbids. Without a single registry (state id → allowed surfaces → required render string → which lint/harness covers it), the shared vocabulary is a suggestion, not a contract maintainers can enforce when tables grow mid-build via fault-induction.

findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 (end-to-end trace artifact schema); Phase 4 — Phase 3 (universal acceptance)
findings.criterion: no dead control; surfaces work E2E or fail with named state — not handler-bound theater
findings.message: Load-bearing honesty rests on `external_observable` being a side effect **outside the process under test** (row / file / pid / network). Many North-Star surfaces (typed attach error UI, projects-collapsed preference, named disabled Diagnose under E1, preview “binary — download”) may have no durable external side effect beyond render. The plan does not say how those controls satisfy the schema without either (a) failing the validator forever, or (b) faking an “external” write that proves nothing about user-visible behavior. Future maintainers under gate pressure will invent process-local stand-ins or mark `capability_call` from direct handler tests — reopening the exact dead-control GREEN path the schema claims to close. Either define per-control allowed observable classes (including render-only with stricter UI proof) before waves, or the schema is overfitted to write-path controls and underfits the NS control set.

findings.topic: inventory invalidation without cheap re-proof path
findings.section: Phase 2 — Phase 1 (evidence expiry; post-change transcript replay)
findings.criterion: nothing wired until real capability exists; dead control forbidden
findings.message: Any commit touching a cited file:line invalidates inventory rows and blocks wave close until transcripts are re-captured. That is right for honesty, but the draft never specifies the re-capture producer after Phase 0 (John live vs replay fixture vs harness), nor how non-semantic edits (import sort, comment, adjacent function) are scoped so invalidation is not noise. Future maintainers will face chronic false invalidation and either stall surface waves (Diagnose never ships) or start closing waves against stale EXISTS rows “because the gate is too expensive” — which is how dead controls return after the inventory looked green. Name the re-proof command, artifact layout, and invalidation granularity (symbol/endpoint, not whole file) or the expiry rule will be bypassed in practice.

findings.topic: terminal status vs never-GREEN E5 criteria
findings.section: Exit register; John-in-the-loop (E5); Phase 6 — Phase 5 status strings
findings.criterion: named user-visible states; S1 is sole NS declaration — not silent “ten criteria met”
findings.message: E5 lets waves proceed with criteria permanently `not verified — awaiting John` / never GREEN, while terminal copy still allows `ten criteria met; North Star pending S1` (or with signed exits). A future status reader — human or tool — cannot tell whether “ten criteria met” means ten GREEN honesty criteria or ten waves closed with unknown surfaces still on screen. That collides with the exit register’s own ban on the unqualified phrase when exits exist, and with the North Star’s requirement that health/usage/diagnose either work E2E or show named failure. If E5-shipped `unknown` attach/Doctor is allowed into “criteria met,” maintainers will report proxy success while John still meets incomplete controls; if it is not allowed, the status grammar never says so. Define whether any never-GREEN criterion forbids the “ten criteria met” token entirely.

findings.criterion: Steward conversational proof is S1, not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: S1 is the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met, yet the draft specifies free-traversal sampling without session duration, minimum surfaces exercised, verdict artifact schema, or positive pass criteria (only “findings” and four blocking classes). A future maintainer (or John on a busy day) cannot distinguish “S1 done, NS met,” “S1 done, NS not met,” and “S1 informal chat, status advanced anyway.” Without a required verdict record shape (`task-name`, `duration`, `surfaces hit`, `blocking findings[]`, `verdict: met|not_met`, signature, date), S1 becomes another escape hatch — either a rubber stamp (silent claim) or an endless reopen with no exit. The North Star’s S1 clause is structural only if pass/fail is as mechanical as a wave gate.

findings.topic: SC-1 single restart vs per-context restart
findings.criterion: open/run/stop/restart without dead control; exactly one restart control per context (as success criteria state)
findings.message: SC bullet 1 requires dead controls eliminated for “a single restart control”; SC bullet 5 requires **exactly one restart control per enumerated restart context** and explicitly rejects cross-context unification. A future wave author implementing “the restart control” will not know whether product-wide singularity or per-context singularity is the acceptance object — and may hide secondary restart affordances or leave duplicates in non-enumerated contexts. That is a dead-control / competing-control defect class the North Star names. Resolve the success criteria so SC-1’s restart clause defers to SC-5’s per-context rule (or vice versa) in one sentence a maintainer can test.

findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 (attestation mechanics); Phase 5 — Phase 4 (cross-check); overview standing rules
findings.criterion: gates that prove E2E honesty — host-computed attestations, not agent claims
findings.message: Honesty depends on “the orchestrator” computing attestation counts, re-running samples, and cross-checking commits — but no binary, script path, or Foreman hook is named. Future maintainers will substitute sub-agent self-reports (the exact failure mode I50 forbids) under time pressure. Name the host process that is allowed to write pass counts into EXECUTION-LOG, or the host-computed rule is non-operational.

findings.topic: SC numbers not bound to bullets
findings.section: Success criteria vs body SC-1…SC-10 references
findings.message: Body text cites SC-1…SC-10 while Success criteria is an unnumbered ten-bullet list. Maintainers will mis-map Doctor vs attach vs gates when filling the traceability matrix. Number the bullets explicitly. (Out-of-scope for severity inflation — documentation hygiene unless it causes wrong-criterion tests.)

Even after renumbering, prefer one scheme (`P0 Ground Truth` … `P5 S1`) everywhere; dual titles invite the collision in Finding 1. Pure maintainability nit if Finding 1 is fixed by deleting one scheme.
